bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: I never see it; at most I wonder at lunch whether the job's requirements were really about the skills or about my age.
bundles.why: It is the recruiter's screen, but I only care that the criteria are job-related and not about age, which I cannot check myself.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When I upload my CV and later read the email and check whether the tool understood my 12 years correctly.
bundles.why: If the tool reads my experience wrongly I will be furious, so I want it to be correct and for a person to be able to fix it, but I do not see it directly.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When I read the rejection on my phone and want to know whether a human or an AI decided I was missing something.
bundles.why: Flags with a reason and a person confirming every decision is the only thing that answers my suspicion that a machine rejected me because of my age.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: I was not shortlisted so I would not get this email, but I would ask a friend who applied whether they had to upload documents.
bundles.why: It does not touch me as a rejected candidate, though it is good that only shortlisted people are bothered.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: At lunch, reading the email on my phone for the first time and deciding in under three minutes whether to complain.
bundles.why: A specific, true reason with the line from my CV is what I need to judge if the decision is fair, and a vague generic one becomes a public complaint.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Never, it is for the HR lead, though I am glad it shows no names.
bundles.why: Totals for the HR lead do not change my situation as a rejected candidate.

proof_timing.why: Handing over certificates and referees before anyone has even read my CV is a lot of effort and risk for a long shot, but after being shortlisted with a stated reason I would gladly do it.
